verdict.reasoning: Both of the claim's factual quotations are accurate, but the defect it alleges is not one. VERIFIED AGAINST THE RENDERS: page 1022 (footer "992 (C)ISO/IEC 2023") does end at "Gujarati:" / "0A81-0A83, 0ABC, 0ABE-0AC5, 0AC7-0AC9, 0ACB-0ACD, 0AE2-0AE3, 0AE6-0AEF," / "0AFA-0AFF" with nothing between that line and the footer; page 1023 (footer "(C)ISO/IEC 2023 993") does open with "Gunjala_Gondi:" over "11D8A-11D8E, 11D90-11D91, 11D93-11D97, 11DA0-11DA9". The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 40822-40830) does read "0AFA-0AFF Gunjala_Gondi:" followed by the page anchor and a block opening on the bare range line. NOTHING IS LOST OR REORDERED. The label "Gunjala_Gondi:" is present, and relative to other CONTENT its position is unchanged: the sequence is still 0AFA-0AFF -> Gunjala_Gondi: -> 11D8A-11D8E... The only things now separating the label from its ranges are furniture lines (the anchor, the "## Page 1023" slice heading, and the running header "# ISO\IEC 1989:2023 (E)"). The claim's stated impact is therefore false: the ranges are NOT "left unattributed" -- the label immediately precedes them in reading order once furniture is discounted, which is exactly how every other cross-page continuation in this annex reads. What actually differs from the PDF is (a) one dropped line break, merging the label onto the preceding range line, and (b) the page to which the label is attributed. That is page-break furniture and line wrapping, which the rejection criteria exclude. SYSTEMATIC, NOT PAGE-SPECIFIC: the identical shape occurs 19 times across the Annex B script tables (e.g. lines 40182 "1E900-1E943, 1E94B Ahom:", 40235 and 40772 "...Buhid:", 40403 "A984-A9B2 Kaithi:", 40876 "...Khojki:", 49087 "...Deseret:", 49431 "...Sinhala:"). Whenever a PDF page's first content line is a short script label, the extraction pipeline hoisted it above the page break and joined it to the previous line. The page-1022 block itself is the mirror image of the complaint: it opens with a headless "1752-1753" precisely because "Buhid:" -- printed as the first line of page 1022 -- was hoisted to the end of the page-1021 block at line 40772. Treating this instance as a structural content defect while the same mechanical artifact stands unremarked 18 other times would misclassify a pipeline pagination quirk as a normative transcription error.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The correct characterization is a cosmetic, systematic pagination artifact of the extraction pipeline: when a PDF page's first content line is a short script label, that label is hoisted above the page break and concatenated onto the last line of the previous page's block. Here "Gunjala_Gondi:" (printed as line 1 of page 1023) was joined to Gujarati's terminal range line as "0AFA-0AFF Gunjala_Gondi:". No text is missing, added, or reordered with respect to other content -- the label still immediately precedes its 11D8A-11D8E, 11D90-11D91, 11D93-11D97, 11DA0-11DA9 ranges once the page anchor and running header are discounted, so the attribution of every code-point range in Annex B remains correct and recoverable. If this is worth logging at all it is a low-severity, whole-document formatting item covering all 19 occurrences (markdown lines 40182, 40235, 40403, 40454, 40506, 40558, 40610, 40772, 40824, 40876, 40928, 40981, 49030, 49087, 49207, 49263, 49319, 49374, 49431) -- reinsert the line break and move the label below the page anchor -- not a per-page structural misplaced-content finding.
